subject: apush
name: AP U.S. History
ced_source: College Board AP U.S. History Course and Exam Description (CED, V.1, 2023 edition), https://apcentral.collegeboard.org/media/pdf/ap-us-history-course-and-exam-description.pdf - used only to read the public unit/topic outline and learning objectives; no exam questions reproduced

topics.title: Contextualizing Period 1
topics.learning_objective: Explain the context for European encounters in the Americas from 1491 to 1607.

topics.title: Native American Societies Before European Contact
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why various native populations in the period before European contact interacted with the natural environment in North America.

topics.title: European Exploration in the Americas
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes of exploration and conquest of the New World by various European nations.

topics.title: Columbian Exchange, Spanish Exploration, and Conquest
topics.learning_objective: Explain causes of the Columbian Exchange and its effect on Europe and the Americas during the period after 1492.

topics.title: Labor, Slavery, and Caste in the Spanish Colonial System
topics.learning_objective: Explain how the growth of the Spanish Empire in North America shaped the development of social and economic structures over time.

topics.title: Cultural Interactions Between Europeans, Native Americans, and Africans
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why European and Native American perspectives of others developed and changed in the period.

topics.title: Causation in Period 1
topics.learning_objective: Explain the effects of the development of transatlantic voyages from 1491 to 1607.

topics.title: Contextualizing Period 2
topics.learning_objective: Explain the context for the colonization of North America from 1607 to 1754.

topics.title: European Colonization in North America
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why various European colonies developed and expanded from 1607 to 1754.

topics.title: The Regions of British Colonies
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why environmental and other factors shaped the development and expansion of various British colonies that developed and expanded from 1607 to 1754.

topics.title: Transatlantic Trade
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of transatlantic trade over time.

topics.title: Interactions Between American Indians and Europeans
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why interactions between various European nations and American Indians changed over time.

topics.title: Slavery in the British Colonies
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of slavery in the various British colonial regions and explain how enslaved peoples responded to slavery.

topics.title: Colonial Society and Culture
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why the movement of a variety of people and ideas across the Atlantic contributed to the development of American culture over time, and how and why the different goals and interests of European leaders and colonists affected how they viewed themselves and their relationship with Britain.

topics.title: Comparison in Period 2
topics.learning_objective: Compare the effects of the development of colonial society in the various regions of North America.

topics.title: Contextualizing Period 3
topics.learning_objective: Explain the context in which America gained independence and developed a sense of national identity.

topics.title: The Seven Years' War (The French and Indian War)
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of the Seven Years' War (the French and Indian War).

topics.title: Taxation Without Representation
topics.learning_objective: Explain how British colonial policies regarding North America led to the Revolutionary War.

topics.title: Philosophical Foundations of the American Revolution
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why colonial attitudes about government and the individual changed in the years leading up to the American Revolution.

topics.title: The American Revolution
topics.learning_objective: Explain how various factors contributed to the American victory in the Revolution.

topics.title: The Influence of Revolutionary Ideals
topics.learning_objective: Explain the various ways the American Revolution affected society; describe the global impact of the American Revolution.

topics.title: The Articles of Confederation
topics.learning_objective: Explain how different forms of government developed and changed as a result of the Revolutionary period.

topics.title: The Constitutional Convention and Debates over Ratification
topics.learning_objective: Explain the differing ideological positions on the structure and function of the federal government.

topics.title: The Constitution
topics.learning_objective: Explain the continuities and changes in the structure and functions of the government with the ratification of the Constitution.

topics.title: Shaping a New Republic
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why competition intensified conflicts among peoples and nations from 1754 to 1800; explain how and why political ideas, institutions, and party systems developed and changed in the new republic.

topics.title: Developing an American Identity
topics.learning_objective: Explain the continuities and changes in American culture from 1754 to 1800.

topics.title: Movement in the Early Republic
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why migration and immigration to and within North America caused competition and conflict over time; explain the continuities and changes in regional attitudes about slavery as it expanded from 1754 to 1800.

topics.title: Continuity and Change in Period 3
topics.learning_objective: Explain how the American independence movement affected society from 1754 to 1800.

units.title: Early Republic: Expansion, Market Revolution and Reform (1800-1848)

topics.title: Contextualizing Period 4
topics.learning_objective: Explain the historical context for the developments of the early republic, 1800-1848.

topics.title: The Rise of Political Parties and the Era of Jefferson
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why political parties developed and changed in the early republic, and the significance of Jefferson's presidency.

topics.title: Politics and Regional Interests
topics.learning_objective: Explain how different regional interests affected politics in the early republic.

topics.title: America on the World Stage
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why U.S. foreign policy developed and changed from 1800 to 1848.

topics.title: Market Revolution: Industrialization
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of industrialization and the transportation and communication revolutions.

topics.title: Market Revolution: Society and Culture
topics.learning_objective: Explain how the Market Revolution changed society, family, gender roles, and class.

topics.title: Expanding Democracy
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why democratic ideas and participation expanded and limits remained.

topics.title: Jackson and Federal Power
topics.learning_objective: Explain how Jackson's presidency affected the balance of power between the federal government, the states, and Native nations.

topics.title: The Development of an American Culture
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why a distinctly American culture developed in the early republic.

topics.title: The Second Great Awakening
topics.learning_objective: Explain how religious movements of the early nineteenth century affected American society.

topics.title: An Age of Reform
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why reform movements developed and the responses to them.

topics.title: African Americans in the Early Republic
topics.learning_objective: Explain how African Americans shaped and responded to slavery and freedom in the early republic.

topics.title: The Society of the South in the Early Republic
topics.learning_objective: Explain how the expansion of cotton and slavery shaped Southern society.

topics.title: Causation in Period 4
topics.learning_objective: Explain causes and effects of continuity and change, expansion, and sectional conflict in the period 1800-1848.

topics.title: Contextualizing Period 5
topics.learning_objective: Explain the context in which sectional conflict emerged from 1844 to 1877.

topics.title: Manifest Destiny
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of westward expansion from 1844 to 1877.

topics.title: The Mexican-American War
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of the Mexican-American War.

topics.title: The Compromise of 1850
topics.learning_objective: Explain the similarities and differences in how regional attitudes affected federal policy in the period after the Mexican-American War.

topics.title: Sectional Conflict: Regional Differences
topics.learning_objective: Explain the effects of immigration from various parts of the world on American culture from 1844 to 1877; explain how regional differences related to slavery caused tension in the years leading up to the Civil War.

topics.title: Failure of Compromise
topics.learning_objective: Explain the political causes of the Civil War.

topics.title: Election of 1860 and Secession
topics.learning_objective: Describe the effects of Lincoln's election.

topics.title: Military Conflict in the Civil War
topics.learning_objective: Explain the various factors that contributed to the Union victory in the Civil War.

topics.title: Government Policies During the Civil War
topics.learning_objective: Explain how Lincoln's leadership during the Civil War impacted American ideals over the course of the war.

topics.title: Reconstruction
topics.learning_objective: Explain the effects of government policy during Reconstruction on society from 1865 to 1877.

topics.title: Failure of Reconstruction
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why Reconstruction resulted in continuity and change in regional and national understandings of what it meant to be American.

topics.title: Comparison in Period 5
topics.learning_objective: Compare the relative significance of the effects of the Civil War on American values.

units.title: The Gilded Age: Industrialization and Its Challenges (1865-1898)

topics.title: Contextualizing Period 6
topics.learning_objective: Explain the historical context for the rise of industrial capitalism in the United States.

topics.title: Westward Expansion: Economic Development
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of the settlement of the West from 1877 to 1898 (economic development).

topics.title: Westward Expansion: Social and Cultural Development
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of the settlement of the West from 1877 to 1898 (social and cultural development, including effects on American Indians).

topics.title: The "New South"
topics.learning_objective: Explain how various factors contributed to continuity and change in the "New South" from 1877 to 1898.

topics.title: Technological Innovation
topics.learning_objective: Explain the effects of technological advances in the development of the United States over time.

topics.title: The Rise of Industrial Capitalism
topics.learning_objective: Explain the socioeconomic continuities and changes associated with the growth of industrial capitalism from 1865 to 1898.

topics.title: Labor in the Gilded Age
topics.learning_objective: Explain the socioeconomic continuities and changes associated with the growth of industrial capitalism from 1865 to 1898 (labor).

topics.title: Immigration and Migration in the Gilded Age
topics.learning_objective: Explain how cultural and economic factors affected migration patterns over time.

topics.title: Responses to Immigration in the Gilded Age
topics.learning_objective: Explain the various responses to immigration in the period over time.

topics.title: Development of the Middle Class
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes of increased economic opportunity and its effects on society.

topics.title: Reform in the Gilded Age
topics.learning_objective: Explain how different reform movements responded to the rise of industrial capitalism in the Gilded Age.

topics.title: Controversies over the Role of Government in the Gilded Age
topics.learning_objective: Explain continuities and changes in the role of the government in the U.S. economy.

topics.title: Politics in the Gilded Age
topics.learning_objective: Explain the similarities and differences between the political parties during the Gilded Age.

topics.title: Continuity and Change in Period 6
topics.learning_objective: Explain the extent to which industrialization brought change from 1865 to 1898.

units.title: Progressive Era, Imperialism, World Wars and the Interwar Years (1890-1945)

topics.title: Contextualizing Period 7
topics.learning_objective: Explain the context in which industrialization, urbanization, migration, and political reform shaped the United States from 1890 to 1945.

topics.title: Imperialism: Debates
topics.learning_objective: Explain the various military, economic, and cultural motivations for and debates about U.S. imperialism in the period from 1890 to 1945.

topics.title: The Spanish-American War
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of the Spanish-American War and the resulting U.S. overseas expansion.

topics.title: The Progressives
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes, goals, and effects of the Progressive movement and its reforms.

topics.title: World War I: Military and Diplomacy
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of U.S. involvement in World War I and the debate over the peace settlement.

topics.title: World War I: Home Front
topics.learning_objective: Explain how the United States mobilized for World War I and how the war affected civil liberties, labor, and society at home.

topics.title: 1920s: Innovations in Communication and Technology
topics.learning_objective: Explain how new technologies, mass production, and consumer culture changed American life in the 1920s.

topics.title: 1920s: Cultural and Political Controversies
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of cultural and political conflict in the 1920s, including nativism, Prohibition, and the Harlem Renaissance.

topics.title: The Great Depression
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of the Great Depression and responses to it.

topics.title: The New Deal
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes, programs, and effects of the New Deal and the debate over government's role.

topics.title: Interwar Foreign Policy
topics.learning_objective: Explain the ways in which U.S. foreign policy between the world wars reflected internationalism, isolationism, and economic interests.

topics.title: World War II: Mobilization
topics.learning_objective: Explain how the United States mobilized its economy and society for World War II and how the war affected groups at home.

topics.title: World War II: Military
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of the major military and diplomatic decisions of the United States in World War II.

topics.title: Postwar Diplomacy
topics.learning_objective: Explain how the Allied wartime and postwar agreements shaped the international order and the origins of the Cold War.

topics.title: Comparison in Period 7
topics.learning_objective: Compare the ways in which Americans responded to changes in the period from 1890 to 1945 across time and across groups and regions.

units.title: Cold War America and the Postwar Era (1945-1980)

topics.title: Contextualizing Period 8
topics.learning_objective: Explain the context for societal change from 1945 to 1980.

topics.title: The Cold War from 1945 to 1980
topics.learning_objective: Explain the continuities and changes in Cold War policies from 1945 to 1980.

topics.title: The Red Scare
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of the Red Scare after World War II.

topics.title: Economy after 1945
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes of economic growth in the years after World War II and the causes and effects of the migration of various groups of Americans after 1945.

topics.title: Culture after 1945
topics.learning_objective: Explain how mass culture has been maintained or challenged over time.

topics.title: Early Steps in the Civil Rights Movement (1940s and 1950s)
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why the civil rights movements developed and expanded from 1945 to 1960.

topics.title: America as a World Power
topics.learning_objective: Explain the various military and diplomatic responses to international developments over time.

topics.title: The Vietnam War
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of the Vietnam War and how and why opposition to existing policies developed.

topics.title: The Great Society
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of continuing policy debates about the role of the federal government, and continuities and changes in immigration patterns.

topics.title: The African American Civil Rights Movement (1960s)
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why various groups responded to calls for the expansion of civil rights from 1960 to 1980, and the federal government's responses.

topics.title: The Civil Rights Movement Expands
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why various groups responded to calls for the expansion of civil rights from 1960 to 1980.

topics.title: Youth Culture of the 1960s
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why opposition to existing policies and values developed and changed over the course of the 1960s and 1970s.

topics.title: The Environment and Natural Resources from 1968 to 1980
topics.learning_objective: Explain how and why policies related to the environment developed and changed from 1968 to 1980.

topics.title: Society in Transition
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of continuing policy debates about the role of the federal government over time.

topics.title: Continuity and Change in Period 8
topics.learning_objective: Explain the continuities and changes in American society, politics, and foreign policy from 1945 to 1980.

units.title: Contemporary America: Conservatism to the Present (1980-Present)

topics.title: Contextualizing Period 9
topics.learning_objective: Explain the context in which the United States faced international and domestic challenges after 1980.

topics.title: Reagan and Conservatism
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of continuing policy debates about the role of the federal government over time.

topics.title: The End of the Cold War
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of the end of the Cold War and its legacy.

topics.title: A Changing Economy
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of economic and technological change over time.

topics.title: Migration and Immigration in the 1990s and 2000s
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of migration patterns over time.

topics.title: Challenges of the 21st Century
topics.learning_objective: Explain the causes and effects of the domestic and international challenges the United States has faced in the 21st century.

topics.title: Causation in Period 9
topics.learning_objective: Explain the relative significance of the effects of change in the period after 1980 on American national identity.
